title: Evals Signal Hub + Ops Subscriptions (Slack & PagerDuty integration)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood's evals system surface regressions when model or config changes land, but there is inconsistent operational signal for on-call teams. Alerts either flood channels with similar failures or collapse unrelated regressions together due to naïve grouping. Customers and internal SREs need a deterministic, low-noise way to consume eval-driven quality signals tied to model/config rollouts.

This ticket scopes a new "Evals Signal Hub" in Console plus an Ops Subscriptions model that wires high-priority eval regressions into Slack and PagerDuty with configurable deduplication and severity mapping. The Hub will be the canonical place to inspect which rollout (model version / quantization / runtime profile / config change) triggered the signal and will store a compact signature to enable dedupe across channels and time windows.

Goals:
- Deliver a Console page (Signal Hub) that links eval regression events to the exact change (model version + config snapshot + rollout id).
- Provide Ops Subscriptions for teams to subscribe to signal categories and tune routing (Slack channel, PagerDuty service, severity thresholds).
- Implement dedupe logic: signature-based grouping + time-window suppression + optional sticky alert ownership to avoid duplicates across channels.
- Ensure alerts include reproducible context: failing prompt examples, delta metrics, recent rollout diffs, and a link to the rollout and PR.

Non-goals:
- Replacing the eval scoring backend — this changes only the event plumbing and Console UX.
- Building a full incident management UI (we will link to PD incidents and Slack threads).

Scope and deliverables:
- Backend event enrichment pipeline: annotate eval regressions with change metadata and compute a stable signature for dedupe.
- Console Signal Hub UI: timeline of regression events, filterable by model, change id, severity, and team-owned subscription.
- Ops Subscriptions UI: create, edit, and preview subscription rules; mapping rules to Slack channels and PagerDuty services; test/send preview message.
- Alert sink integrations: Slack message formatter + PagerDuty events v2 integration; webhooks for enterprise customers who use custom sinks.
- Deduplication algorithm: a configurable window (default 30m), signature hash (model+config+promptset+top-k failing buckets), and sticky owner assignment while alert is open.

Why now:
- Several production incidents in Q4 and Q1 where model rollouts caused correlated regressions and on-call fatigue (see postmortem RFC: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/PM-EVALS-incident-2025-11).
- Customer asks for improved observability and fewer false-positive alerts in PagerDuty.

User stories:
- As an SRE, I want only one PD incident per unique regression signature during a rollout so I can focus on root cause without chasing duplicates.
- As a PM, I want to subscribe the model team Slack channel to high-severity eval regressions for their model so they can triage quickly.
- As a support engineer, I want to click from an alert to the failing prompt and the exact config diff so I can reproduce and file a fix.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Console Signal Hub page implemented behind feature flag and lists enriched eval events with linked change ID and PR link.
2) Subscriptions can map events to Slack channels and PagerDuty services, and send preview messages.
3) Deduplication reduces duplicate PagerDuty incidents for identical regression signatures in a 30 minute window by >= 80% in internal test harness.
4) Each alert contains context: top 3 failing prompts, metric delta, model version, config snapshot ref, rollout id, and a permalink to the eval result.
5) E2E test (integration) demonstrates Slack message -> PD incident creation -> suppressed duplicate event within window.

Success metrics:
- Reduce PD duplicate incidents caused by eval regressions by 80% compared to baseline (measured over two weeks after rollout).
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for eval regression incidents improves by 30% for teams using subscriptions.
- Less than 5% of high-severity eval signals flagged as 'noise' in post-implementation survey.

Design links:
- Signal Hub mockups (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/REDWOOD-EVALS/signal-hub-prototypes
- Subscription UI flows: https://www.figma.com/file/REDWOOD-EVALS/subscriptions-flows
- Slack/PagerDuty message templates: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/evals/alerts/templates

Engineering links:
- Event enrichment RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/198
- Dedupilation PoC (python): https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals-dedupe-poc
- Backend PR for enrichment pipeline (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8173

Dependencies:
- ENG-20577 (eval regression telemetry attribution) — needs merging for attribution fields.
- ENG-21901 (console auth + new page routing) — small console router change required.
- Security review for PD integration (KMS and secret handling).

Release: "console-2026.04"
Security_review_required: true

Risks and mitigation:
- Over-aggregation: different regressions could be collapsed if signature too coarse. Mitigation: provide adjustable signature granularity and an "unwrap grouped events" action in UI.
- Too many subscriptions: could cause notification storms. Mitigation: preview channel messages and default rate-limits per subscription.
- Enterprise PD mapping differences: provide webhook sink and templating for advanced customers.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Backend enrichment + dedupe worker prototype (internal alpha).
- Week 2: Console Signal Hub basic UI + subscription create/edit flow behind feature flag.
- Week 3: Slack + PagerDuty integration + preview + integration tests.
- Week 4: Gradual opt-in for internal teams -> refine thresholds -> external beta with 2 customers.

Analytics & observability:
- Track events emitted to sinks, dedupe actions taken, subscription count, PD incidents created and optional mapping to incidents that triggered pagerduty on-call escalations.
- Telemetry dashboard for product to inspect false-positive rates and subscription health.
